name: Dolphin
intro: A dolphin is a smart animal that lives in the water. It is a mammal, not a fish.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A dolphin has smooth, rubbery skin.
It has flippers, a tail, and a back fin.
Many dolphins are gray.
It breathes air through a blowhole on top of its head.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Dolphins live in oceans all around the world.
Some kinds of dolphins live in rivers.
Bottlenose dolphins like warm water.
Some swim near the shore.
Some swim far out at sea.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Dolphins eat fish and squid.
Some dolphins eat shrimp, too.
Dolphins work together to catch fish.
They make clicks and listen for echoes to find food.
They swallow fish head first.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby dolphin is called a calf.
A mother dolphin usually has one calf at a time.
The calf is born in the water, tail first.
The mother feeds her calf milk for a long time.
Dolphins live in groups called pods.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Each dolphin has its own whistle, like a name.
A dolphin sleeps with half of its brain at a time.
Each dolphin eye can move on its own.
Dolphins like to play and ride on waves.
A bottlenose dolphin can know itself in a mirror.

vocab.meaning: An animal that breathes air and feeds its babies milk.
A hole on top of the head for breathing.
A sound that bounces back to you.
A group of dolphins or whales.
